incident-bot: :rotating_light: NEW INCIDENT: eu-central GPU pool 'eu-central-infer' showing sustained request queue growth, autoscaler hit scale-limit, placement failures. Severity P1. Pager: @leah (oncall).

leah (oncall): Paging infra. Console shows queue at ~1200 pending, 95th latency >8s. Autoscaler logs: repeated 'placement failed: insufficient contiguous MIG capacity'. Looks like fragmentation after last night's MIG reprofile.

ben (sre): I'm pulling scheduler and node reports. Autoscaler attempted to spin up 18 nodes but stopped due to account scale cap. Also seeing many nodes with small leftover MIG fragments (2g, 3g) that cannot satisfy 8g requirements. Posting snippet:
```
[2026-04-02T03:12:14Z] scheduler: placement failure: pod req=1xA100-80G-mig-8g, nodes_checked=27, contiguous_free=0
[2026-04-02T03:12:20Z] autoscaler: scale_attempts=18, reason=scale_limit_reached
```

carmen (runtime): Confirmed on node inventory: half the pool is mixed 8g/4g/1g profiles. The latest node image left some devices reprofiled incorrectly, leaving non-contiguous free MIG slices. Our placement policy refuses to split across fragments.

paul (eng): Customer impact? Are any production customers getting 5xx?

leah (oncall): We're returning 429 throttles intermittently and some timeouts. CS alerted. Prioritization: keep SLA customers on dedicated reserved capacity, degrade non-SLA first.

maria (cs): I'm drafting messages. Early list: DataFi (prod), HealthKit (prod), RetailAI (staging). Will send an update now and flag execs for DataFi.

ben (sre): Short term options I see: bump account scale limit (if allowed), enable fragment-coalescing scheduler mode to pack across fragments for non-critical pools, or perform live reprovision to normalize MIG profiles. Each has tradeoffs.

leah (oncall): We need to act quickly. Carmen, can runtime flip a temporary "fragment_coalesce" mode to allow placing pods across smaller slices for inference types that tolerate slight perf hit?

carmen (runtime): We have a gate: `scheduler.fragment_coalesce_enabled`. I can enable it for eu-central-infer and exclude high-priority tenant labels. Doing it now:
```
./adminctl flags set eu-central-infer scheduler.fragment_coalesce_enabled true --reason "incident: reduce queue" --expires 45m
```

deploy-bot: flag-change: scheduler.fragment_coalesce_enabled toggled ON for eu-central-infer by carmen. Change id: fc-20260402-01

ben (sre): Flag is on. Kicking off emergency compact/rebalance job to migrate low-priority pods onto fragmented nodes so higher-req pods get contiguous capacity: 
```
compact --pool eu-central-infer --mode live --concurrency 6 --target-label "tier!=sla"
```

leah (oncall): Running. Watch for eviction storms. Keep concurrency limited. Also, can we temporarily increase autoscaler soft-limit to allow additional nodes while rebalance runs?

paul (eng): I can request temporary bump from infra quota team. Submitting request now with justification and expected duration 2h.

ben (sre): Real-time update: rebalance moved ~320 pods in 12 minutes. Queue dropped from 1200 -> 380. Tail latency down to ~3.4s. Still ~90 pods pending due to shortage of 8g MIG slots.

maria (cs): Messaging update sent to DataFi and HealthKit: "We're mitigating an infrastructure fragmentation issue affecting inference throughput; mitigation underway and performance improving." Both acknowledged.

leah (oncall): If quota bump is delayed, we should prepare node reprovision plan: cordon small-fragment nodes and reprovision them with uniform 8g profile. This will be disruptive but may be necessary. Recommend scheduling cordon in waves.

carmen (runtime): I will prepare a non-disruptive reprovision helper that attempts live reassignments before drain. It'll mark nodes with label `reprofile=pending` and avoid evicting high-priority pods. Example: 
```
./nodes reprofile --pool eu-central-infer --from-mig-scheme mixed --to-scheme uniform-8g --batch-size 4 --evict-filter "tier!=sla"
```

ben (sre): Good. Also adding a temporary autoscaler policy override for rebalance: `autoscaler.allow_overprovision=true` while compact job runs. Leah, please coordinate with quota if you need official sign-off.

leah (oncall): On-call handoff note for the 07:00 UTC shift: I've enabled fragment coalesce, started compact job (id fc-20260402-01), requested quota bump, and prepped reprovision script. Monitor the queue and autoscaler errors. Key runbook commands:
```
# check flag
./adminctl flags get eu-central-infer scheduler.fragment_coalesce_enabled
# compact status
compact status --id fc-20260402-01
# reprovision simulation
./nodes reprofile --dry-run --pool eu-central-infer
```

paul (eng): ACK. Taking handoff at 03:55 UTC. I'll follow up on the quota request and coordinate reprovision if needed.

ben (sre): Compact finished first phase: 560 pods relocated, freed 14 contiguous 8g-equivalents. Queue is now 60 and dropping. Latency back to baseline for most tenants. 10 pods remain pending due to large memory requests.

maria (cs): Customer update: "Systems are recovering; we will follow up with a post-incident summary." DataFi thanks the team.

carmen (runtime): I'll open tickets for: 1) add fragmentation alert (high ratio of fragmented free slices), 2) add auto-reprofile step in node upgrade pipeline, 3) make fragment coalesce toggle safer (auto-exclude SLA tenants).

ben (sre): Preliminary root cause: partial node reprofiles during maintenance left mixed MIG layouts; autoscaler and placement policy require contiguous slots for some pod classes, producing stranded capacity and preventing autoscaler from satisfying demands.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: queue reduced to baseline, 98% queued requests processed. Mitigations: fragment_coalesce flag + compact + reprovision plan. Incident duration ~46m. Severity: P1 -> mitigated. Postmortem assigned to runtime + infra.

maria (cs): I'll consolidate customer notes and post a timeline.

leah (oncall): Handoff complete. Leaving notes in the tracker: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2406123456. Please ensure action items get scheduled. Great teamwork.
